name: Building Energy Benchmarking and Performance Standard Requirements by Jurisdiction
description: Which US cities and states require commercial buildings to report annual energy consumption, the square footage threshold above which reporting is mandatory, the annual reporting deadline, whether emissions reduction targets or performance standards apply, penalty amounts for noncompliance, and the governing ordinance citation. Over 50 jurisdictions have adopted requirements as of 2026, with new ones every year.

records.performance_standard: 7% reduction by 2026 and 20% by 2030, compared to 2021 levels
records.penalty_noncompliance: Late reports and fees are subject to penalties
records.source_quote: Building Performance Colorado Benchmarking and building performance standards to reduce emissions statewide. The state’s Building Performance Colorado (BPC) program, which includes benchmarking requirements and Building Performance Standards (BPS), will help meet State goals to reduce emissions from the commercial buildings sector by 7% by 2026 and 20% by 2030, compared to 2021 levels. These policies apply to most commercial buildings 50,000 square feet and larger (“covered buildings”). Benchmarking requirements increase transparency for how buildings use energy and help building owners: Reduce emissions from the building sector Reduce energy and operating costs Prioritize investments in energy upgrades and building improvements <https://cogov.tfaforms.net/292> Sign up for updates on the BPC Program Key Dates and Deadlines for Covered Buildings July 1, annually: Benchmarking reporting period opens. November 1, annually: Benchmarking report and fee payment due. Late reports and fees are subject to penalties.
